question: What does a full RefSeq Enterobacterales run cost and find, on one 16-core / 56 GB box?

run.settings: pepm_prescreen on, recover_orfs on, GTDB-Tk on, 10 kb neighbourhood, download_batch_size 25, download_max_forks 2

the_cpu_shape_has_inverted.why_it_matters: On Erwiniaceae antiSMASH was 81.5% of CPU and every sizing note in CLAUDE.md follows from that. Here it is 29%, and fetching-and-screening is the largest single consumer -- because the screen rejects 99.1% and antiSMASH only ever sees 1,309 genomes. At order scale this pipeline is no longer antiSMASH-bound.
the_cpu_shape_has_inverted.the_stage_nobody_modelled: RECOVER_ORFS is 20% of CPU and appeared in none of the projections given before this run.

peak_disk_measured_not_projected.observed_peak: 150 GB total consumed; outdir 30 GB, work 150 GB
peak_disk_measured_not_projected.where_it_actually_went: 111 GB of the peak is a single GTDBTK_CLASSIFY task, 95 GB of that being pplacer scratch. That is set by GTDB's reference data, not by how few genomes reach it.
peak_disk_measured_not_projected.what_the_storage_work_did_and_did_not_do: The output directory behaved exactly as designed: 30 GB, with the screened-out 99.1% never written. What was wrong was generalising that to 'peak disk'. Peak no longer tracks TAXON SIZE -- it tracks GTDB-Tk. Those are different claims and CLAUDE.md asserted the weaker one as though it were the stronger.

download.rate: 70.4 genomes/min sustained, against 98 measured in the Erwiniaceae soak
download.why_slower: The soak cycled a 2,784-accession Erwiniaceae pool containing 213 Buchnera endosymbionts at ~0.6 Mb. Enterobacterales is full of 5-6 Mb Klebsiella and E. coli, so bytes per genome are higher. 98/min was a clade-specific figure generalised too freely.
download.failures: 0 tasks failed across 6,028 fetch batches. The ~8% invalid-zip rate measured in the soak was absorbed by the three inline retries; the per-accession fallback is not known to have fired.

chemistry.reading: 1,069 of 1,303 BGCs are not within 0.30 of ANY characterised cluster, including all 12 pepM-bearing MIBiG entries. Note the nearest non-pantaphos distances are much shorter here than on Erwiniaceae (0.37-0.43 against 0.62-0.89), so the order does contain chemistry closer to the known record -- just not inside the family cutoff.
chemistry.branch_points: not via PnAA 30, unknown (Ppd, no third enzyme) 24, 2-AEP 13, 2-HEP 3, unknown (Ppd + class I/II transaminase) 2

the_pilot_retraction_was_right: The 640-genome pilot gave 40 GCFs from 50 BGCs, 34 of them singletons, and an early reading took that as high diversity. It was dereplication: one genome per species. At full depth the same order gives 72 families from 1,303 BGCs with a largest of 186 and only 16 singletons -- families accumulate members exactly as predicted.

prevalence_projection_vs_measurement.erwiniaceae_rates_borrowed: 11% screen retention, 10.8% BGC-positive -- would have predicted ~16,500 genomes to antiSMASH
prevalence_projection_vs_measurement.reading: The clade-aware model was right in shape and conservative in degree. The flat Erwiniaceae rate was wrong by 12x, and wrong on the stage that binds.

data.disk_samples.tsv: 60 s samples of free/outdir/work/memory across the whole run -- peak only exists during a run, and du afterwards measures the residue
data.pipeline_trace.tsv.gz: per-task Nextflow trace, the basis of the CPU table above
data.prescreen_verdicts.tsv.gz: every one of the 150,682 screen decisions
